text:
ashwin: Heads up — hitting a weird auth+okhttp connection affinity issue in the Kotlin SDK sample app on Android 14/15. Repro steps attached.

laura: ugh, details?

ashwin: app uses Retrofit + OkHttp, interceptor does synchronous token refresh when 401, we relied on Connection: keep-alive. under load a bunch of queued requests end up on the same connection and the token refresh blocks the dispatcher -> requests stall and client retries, causing 401 loops.

olivia: can you paste the interceptor code?

ashwin: here —
```kotlin
class TokenInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request()
    val token = tokenProvider.get() // may block while refreshing
    val newReq = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
    val resp = chain.proceed(newReq)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      tokenProvider.refreshSync() // synchronous refresh
      val retried = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenProvider.get()}").build()
      return chain.proceed(retried)
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```

kevin: That pattern is risky on Android. OkHttp uses limited concurrent streams per connection and if the refresh blocks it can starve the connection's stream queue. We've seen similar with synchronous authenticators.

laura: Did you try using an Authenticator instead of an Interceptor for 401? Authenticator runs on a dedicated thread pool I think.

ashwin: We tried authenticator but hit a different repro: when the authenticator does a synchronous call to refresh token it re-enters OkHttp and deadlocks (since same client used). So we get stack traces like: 
```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: cannot make recursive call
 at okhttp3.internal.connection.RealCall.testRecurse(RealCall.java:XXX)
 at okhttp3.Call.execute(RealCall.java:YYY)
```
olivia: yeah classic. Best practice is: token refresh should be performed out-of-band (separate OkHttp client without interceptors) or be async and coordinate single-flight refresh.

ashwin: confirmed. Quick mitigation: replace synchronous refresh with a suspend-based singleflight that only does one network call and others wait, and use a separate OkHttp client for that refresh. Fix cut into sample app.

kevin: can you add a small reproducer snippet to the repo? We should also add a doc note in the SDK "Auth best practices" page. Mention Android dispatcher limits and connection affinity.

ashwin: will open PR with repro and docs. PR will include: small sample app change, README update, and a test that simulates 20 concurrent requests.

laura: also add a short blurb for on-call: how to recognize (stack traces, many queued calls on same connection, repeated 401 + refresh spikes).

infra-bot: reminder: new SDK alpha 3.6.0-alpha1 published with okHttp update and improved default dispatcher.

ashwin: nice — will validate patch against alpha. thanks all. :thumbsup:
